one_month_reasoning: No Dycom earnings fall inside the window to 2026-11-08: Q3 FY2027 (quarter ends Oct 31) should report in the second half of November (prior-year Q3 released 2025-11-19, src 7, 12). In-window events are read-throughs and macro: (1) late-October Q3 reports and capex commentary from AT&T (20.1% of Q2 revenue) and Verizon (10.4%) (src 3); (2) MasTec/Quanta Q3 reports (MasTec Q2 Communications margin fell 170bp to 8.2%, src 32, so its Q3 segment margin is the most direct read-through); (3) hyperscaler capex guidance in late October; (4) the Oct 27-28 FOMC (~16% hike odds on Kalshi/Polymarket per the DeFi Rate snapshot, src 26). None gives a clear directional edge. The stock sits near its 52-week low after a -2.9% day on Oct 9 (src 27); short-term reversal and continued momentum roughly cancel, and the CEO's September open-market buy (850 sh at $296.76, src 33) is too small to be a signal. So I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred on ~$269.5 with monthly sigma 15% (52% annual / 3.5). Unchanged from round 1 apart from rounding: none of the supervisor's findings concerns an in-window event.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM adjusted P/E ($21.38 calendar-weighted NTM EPS at Oct-2027 x 16.0x = $342, 50%), NTM EV/EBITDA ($1,264M x 10x less $2.57B lease-inclusive net debt over 30.4M shares = $331, 40%) and a re-based FCF yield ($12.47/share underlying FCF at 6% = $208, 10%): 171 + 132.4 + 20.8 = ~$324.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis forecast page, 'EPS Next Year 20.78 from 17.05' (the 'This Year' figure 17.05 matches the FY Jan-2027 column, so 'Next Year' is FY Jan-2028).
Consistent with H1 actual $9.71 (src 1) + Q3 guide midpoint $4.56 (src 1) + implied Q4 ~$2.78.

$20.78 x 1.12 = $23.27. 12% is below consensus FY28 revenue growth of 13.2% ($8.58B vs $7.58B, src 13) and the 27.3% 3Y EPS growth forecast (src 14) because implied H2 FY27 Communications revenue is roughly flat; backlog $12.24B (+53%) and next-12-month backlog $6.47B (src 2) support continued growth.
FY28 ends ~Jan 29, 2028 (src 13 fiscal-year table: FY ends late January); Oct 9, 2027 to Jan 29, 2028 is ~112 days / 365 = 0.31 of a year left in FY28. Round 1 used 0.25/0.75.
0.31 x 20.78 + 0.69 x 23.27 = 6.44 + 16.06 = $22.50; haircut 5% for the risk that Communications re-acceleration in FY28 disappoints (H2 FY27 implied Communications ~-1% YoY, src 1, 2) = $21.38.

MTZ, the closest telecom-contractor peer, trades at 19.89x forward (src 15); 11-peer median 22.92x, range 15.18x-38.32x (src 15-25). 16.0x is ~20% below MTZ and inside the 11-peer range. The discount rests on three verified, persistent differences: (a) leverage: net debt/TTM EBITDA ~2.90x for DY ($2.70B / $932M, src 14) vs ~2.23x for MTZ ($2.92B / $1.31B, src 15); (b) concentration: AT&T+Verizon+Lumen 35.8% of Q2 revenue (src 3); (c) cash quality: supplier-finance obligations rose from $0 (Jul 26, 2025) to $367.4M (Aug 1, 2026) (src 29) and the FY26 AP increase was $223.2M of $642.5M operating cash flow (src 30). Round 1 used 15.5x and also cited the amortization add-back; that argument is withdrawn because MasTec's 2026 guide is adjusted EPS $9.30 vs GAAP $6.20 (src 32), a wider adjusted/GAAP gap than DY's Q2 $5.29 vs $3.81 (src 1). Removing that reason and adding the cash-quality reason nets to a slightly smaller discount: 16.0x. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Gate-derived (Oct-9 close / calendarised NTM consensus EPS): MTZ 18.18x, 8-peer median 22.01x (7 with a consensus source; IESC none), 11-peer median 21.61x (range 11.40x LMB to 37.00x PWR); DY 13.72x. Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases. The 16x multiple is the agent's judgment and is unchanged; on this basis it is ~12% below MTZ.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at Oct-2027 $1,264M x 10.0x = EV $12.64B; less lease-inclusive net debt $2.57B ($2.34B notional + $0.23B operating leases); / 30.4M diluted shares = $331

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 FY27 margin 14.6% (src 2); Q3 guide midpoint $291.5M / $1.94B = 15.0% (src 1); FY26 13.3% (src 6); held near H1 level given guided slight Communications margin decline (src 2). FY28 EBITDA = 8,583 x 14.5% = $1,245M.
$1,245M x 1.10; EBITDA grown slower than EPS (12%) because part of EPS growth comes from lower interest as debt is repaid.
0.31 x 1,245 + 0.69 x 1,369 = $1,330M, less the same 5% haircut as the P/E leg = $1,264M.

DY today: lease-inclusive EV $10.82B / TTM EBITDA $932M = 11.6x (src 14), ~9.0x on NTM EBITDA (~0.31 x FY27 ~$1.09B + 0.69 x FY28 $1.245B = ~$1.20B; FY27 = H1 $578M src 1 + Q3 guide mid $291.5M src 1 + Q4 ~$216M). 10x NTM is ~12.8x trailing-equivalent: below MTZ's 15.12x trailing (src 15) and the bottom of the 11-peer trailing range 11.02x-36.86x for the leverage/concentration/cash-quality reasons in the P/E leg. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Filings-based trailing EV/EBITDA: MTZ 14.58x (company-adjusted TTM), 8-peer median 19.32x (range 14.58x MTZ to 36.64x PWR), 11-peer median 17.68x (range 11.25x LMB to 36.64x PWR); DY 11.28x (EV $10.83B / adjusted TTM EBITDA $959.8M). The multiple is the agent's judgment and is unchanged.
Q2 presentation notional net debt (src 2). Cross-check from XBRL (src 30): cash $340.1M; carrying debt $28.4M current + $2,791.3M long-term = $2,819.7M; carrying net debt $2,479.6M.

$2,502.6M - ~$290M underlying FCF over ~14 months + ~$75M buybacks + ~$50M tuck-in M&A = $2,338M. Underlying FCF ~$250M/yr is anchored on FY26 FCF $435.3M (src 6) less the $223.2M FY26 AP increase (src 30) = $212M, grown with earnings; it excludes any further supplier-finance build (src 29). Buybacks: $83.9M was left on the old $150M program at Aug 1, 2026 (10-Q, src 3) and management announced a new $150M authorization (src 4). Round 1 used ~$2.2B, which leaned on supplier-finance-flattered FCF.

inputs_detail.input: Operating lease liability (added because the 10x anchor uses StockAnalysis lease-inclusive EV)
inputs_detail.derivation: XBRL OperatingLeaseLiability at Aug 1, 2026 (10-Q). Matches StockAnalysis total debt $3.05B (src 14) less carrying debt $2.82B. Lease-inclusive horizon net debt = 2,338 + 229 = $2,567M.
Q2 FY27 weighted diluted shares 30,363,819 (src 1, XBRL src 30).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Re-based: FY28 FCF = adj. NI $632M x 60% underlying conversion = $379M = $12.47/share at a 6.0% yield = $208

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 FCF $435.3M (src 6) less FY26 accounts-payable increase $223.2M (src 30) = $212.1M; FY26 adjusted NI = FY26 adjusted EPS $11.97 (src 13) x 29.42M FY26 diluted shares (src 30) = $352.2M; 212.1 / 352.2 = 60%. Round 1 used 85% on reported FCF, which the supplier-finance build ($0 to $367.4M, src 29) flattered.
Current TTM FCF yield 5.77% on reported FCF (src 14); 6% reflects leverage and rate-hike risk (src 26).

bear.story: Communications stays flat-to-down into FY28 (H2 FY27 implied ~-1% YoY), the $150M wireless deferral slips again, BEAD construction is delayed, AI/hyperscaler capex cools, the supplier-finance build ($367.4M) reverses and pulls FCF toward zero, and rate hikes pressure contractor multiples: FY28 EPS ~$17 x ~11x.

base.story: FY28 outlook (early Mar-2027) near consensus with Communications re-accelerating on the wireless catch-up, BEAD and long-haul backlog; Building Systems grows; NTM EPS ~$21-22 at ~14.5x, as the market keeps a leverage/concentration/cash-quality discount and does not yet pay the full 16x.

bull.story: Backlog conversion ($12.2B, +53%) drives beats and a strong FY28 outlook, H2 FCF de-levers without further payables stretch, and the multiple re-rates toward ~19-20x NTM EPS (MTZ's level).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount must persist through Oct-2027 and rests on verified structural differences only: (1) leverage: net debt/TTM EBITDA ~2.90x for DY ($2.70B / $932M, src 14) vs ~2.23x for MTZ ($2.92B / $1.31B, src 15), after the Power Solutions deal; de-leveraging is slow because underlying FCF ex-payables build is ~$212M (src 6, 30); (2) concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of Q2 revenue (src 3); (3) cash quality: supplier-finance obligations went from $0 to $367.4M in a year (src 29) and receivables are sold non-recourse to a customer's bank partner (10-Q, src 3). Withdrawn from round 1: the amortization add-back argument, because MasTec's adjusted/GAAP gap ($9.30 vs $6.20, src 32) is wider than DY's. DY's 3Y EPS growth forecast (27.3%, src 14) is mid-pack, so no growth-based discount is applied, which is why 16x stays inside the 11-peer range. Going below the 8-peer range is justified because none of those eight carries DY's combination of ~2.9x leverage and 36% three-customer concentration. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is ~9.6x FY28 consensus EPS of $20.78 (src 13), ~26% below today and ~24% below the $263.36 52-week low; trading there would most likely mean an earnings reset (FY28 outlook in early Mar-2027 with Communications still declining after the wireless recapture, an AT&T/Verizon program cut, Building Systems margins collapsing from 24.5%) or a cash-flow problem (the $367.4M supplier-finance build reversing and pulling FCF negative), not ordinary 52%-vol noise. Covenant stress is not a near-term channel: the maximum consolidated net leverage covenant is 4.50x (stepping to 4.00x later) with 2.50x minimum interest coverage, the company was in compliance at Aug 1, 2026 and had $746.4M revolver availability (10-Q, src 3), vs ~2.3x pro forma leverage.

reasoning: Dycom fell from a $566.47 high to $269 (14.6x forward, src 14) while FY28 consensus held at $20.78 (src 13): a de-rating on a slowing Communications run-rate (implied H2 FY27 Communications ~flat, $150M wireless deferral to FY28, margin outlook to 'slight decline'), not an estimate cut. Round 2 changes after the supervisor's review, each re-checked at source: (1) the supplier-finance build is real (XBRL: $0 -> $367.4M, src 29; FY26 AP +$223.2M of $642.5M OCF, src 30), so my FCF leg is re-based on underlying conversion (60%) and cut to 10% weight ($294 -> $208), and horizon net debt rises from ~$2.2B to $2.34B notional; (2) operating leases ($228.7M, src 31) are added to net debt because my EV/EBITDA anchor is StockAnalysis's lease-inclusive EV; (3) P/E and EV/EBITDA legs move to a calendar-correct NTM basis (0.31 FY28 / 0.69 FY29) and the EV/EBITDA leg from FY28 to NTM EBITDA; (4) the amortization argument for a discount is withdrawn (MTZ adj/GAAP gap is wider, src 32) while cash quality is added, and the P/E target moves from 15.5x to 16.0x; (5) the key-gated Alpha Vantage consensus citation is replaced by the StockAnalysis forecast page (same $20.78/$8.58B, src 13). Net: P/E $333 -> $342, EV/EBITDA $337 -> $331, FCF $294 -> $208; fair value $327 -> $324 (+20%). I keep the 11-peer set (the brief asks for 10-12) but report the supervisor's 8-peer median, which I recomputed myself (23.29x). For the ladder I again shrink toward the market because the downtrend, a likely December hike and the March FY28 outlook risk are real: split lognormal with median ~$287, sigma 0.49 below / 0.46 above (realized vol 52%, part of it a one-way derating), giving P(>=269) ~0.55, slightly below round 1 (0.565) as weaker cash quality offsets the NTM-basis uplift. Scenario mean ~$308. Sources: sec.gov HTML refused scripted access with a generic UA, so the 10-Q and Form 4 were read with WebFetch; data.sec.gov XBRL APIs were reachable with a generic UA (no key). StockAnalysis FY28/FY29 forecast tables are paywalled ('Pro'); only the free 'Next Year' figures are used, and FY29 is my estimate. No option data was consulted.
